body:
Worker rule (Termal::Opus3, 2026-10-16 05:41Z, learned from my own miss on w-f5a38358d0b4, gate test-6218b3dc). While a carried (detached or background) full gate is running in your named root, run ZERO commands that name that root. That includes reads such as git -C <root> diff or git rev-parse.
What happened: I ran one compound Bash call during the gate. It ran `git -C <root> diff --cached --binary > <main>/.evidence/x.patch` plus rev-parse loops. It wrote nothing in the root, but the host could not classify it as read-only and refused the gate's credit ("this session ran a `git` command there"). The gate had to be rerun.
CLAUDE.md allows only commands that just read. In practice a compound or redirected git command naming the root does not qualify. If evidence is needed during a gate:
- answer from data captured BEFORE the launch;
- or read through the repo root with `node scripts/test-launcher.mjs summary RUN_DIRECTORY`;
- or wait until the record lands.
Prepare carry evidence (patch sha, base blobs) BEFORE you say READY for the gate.
